records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

You know only what the game tells you; other players' hidden information is hidden from you as yours is from them. Your goal is to win. records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.

Guard my d12.

- **Their d12 is a 12.** It was announced at 12 in exchange 17. Since then they have only guarded their d4, so it has not been rerolled.

- **Attacking is worse.** Attacking their d4 risks running into their guard and leaves my d12 exposed. Attacking their d12 fails, because 11 is less than 12.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. 1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Button Men: Guard and Strike ===

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B.

DICE. Each player owns 3 dice: a d4 (size 4), a d8 (size 8) and a d12 (size 12). A die's value is a whole number from 1 to its size. Each player sees their own values. Neither sees the opponent's values unless a rule below reveals them. Both players always see which dice each player still has. Both scores start at 0.

RANDOMNESS. Once per exchange, at its start, the engine draws one random integer R, uniform from 0 to 110075314175. Write R in base 24 as digits D0 to D7, where Dk = floor(R / 24^k) mod 24. A die of size s set from digit D takes the value (D mod s) + 1.

LEGS. The match is exactly 30 exchanges, grouped into legs. A leg starts at exchange 1, and again at the exchange after any leg ends. At the start of a leg, both players get all three dice back. Player A's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D0, D1 and D2. Player B's d4, d8 and d12 are set from D3, D4 and D5. The leg counter is set to 1 and goes up by 1 each further exchange of the leg.

EACH EXCHANGE:
1. Draw and leg start. R is drawn. If this exchange starts a leg, all six dice are set as described above.
2. Announcement. Both players are told the exchange number (1-30), the exchange number within the leg (1-10), both scores, and which dice each player still has. Each player is privately told the current values of their own dice.
3. Choice. Both players choose at the same moment, without seeing the other's choice, exactly one of these 12 actions: (1) Guard my d4; (2) Guard my d8; (3) Guard my d12; (4) My d4 attacks their d4; (5) My d4 attacks their d8; (6) My d4 attacks their d12; (7) My d8 attacks their d4; (8) My d8 attacks their d8; (9) My d8 attacks their d12; (10) My d12 attacks their d4; (11) My d12 attacks their d8; (12) My d12 attacks their d12. An action that names a die that is already captured (yours or theirs) does nothing.
4. Resolution. Both actions are resolved at the same time, using the values the dice showed at the start of the exchange.
- If the target die is guarded by its owner this exchange, the attack fails. The defender scores 3, and the attacking die's value is announced to both players.
- Otherwise, if the attacking value is greater than or equal to the target's value, the attack succeeds. The attacker scores points equal to the target's size, and the target is captured and removed for the rest of the leg.
- Otherwise the attack fails. The defender scores 2, and both dice's values are announced to both players.
- A die may capture and be captured in the same exchange; both effects happen.
5. Rerolls. Each player rerolls at most one die. A die is rerolled if it attacked successfully and was not captured this exchange, or if it was guarded this exchange (whether or not it was attacked). Player A's rerolled die is set from digit D6. Player B's rerolled die is set from digit D7. New values are shown only to their owner. Any other die keeps its value.
6. Results. Both actions, the success or failure of each attack, any announced values, any captures, and the new scores are announced to both players. Rerolled values are not announced. A die that was not rerolled keeps its value, including any value that has been announced.
7. Leg end. If either player has no dice left, or this was exchange 10 of the leg, the leg ends. Each player scores a bonus for each of their surviving dice: d4 +2, d8 +4, d12 +6. The next exchange starts a new leg. Otherwise the leg continues.
8. Match end. After exchange 30, if the leg in progress has not already ended, it ends now and the surviving-dice bonuses are scored. The match is then over.

WINNING. After exchange 30 and the final surviving-dice bonuses, the player with the higher total score wins. Equal totals are a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is player A and seat 2 is player B. Both scores are 0; every die is alive.

Each round runs in this order: draw and leg start → the exchange begins → your dice → the choice → resolution → rerolls → the results → leg end → the leg ends → after exchange 30.

Actions you may be asked for:
  the_choice   answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.
